title: The two-branch diagram needs a specified punctured neighborhood
place: central diagram, circled local ring, and final proof request
source_words: Z=Spec; Π₁(Z)=Ẑ²; th. de descente; hom. canoniques
body: Scan107 places the completed local spectrum beside a diagram with Π₁(Z)=Ẑ² and explicitly asks for a local descent theorem and canonical homomorphisms. In the model A=ℂ[[x,y]], every finite étale cover of the full Spec A splits, so its fundamental group is trivial; the boundary complement is a different space and must be specified before invoking a two-generator inertia calculation. Hua repeats the diagram and links it to earlier completions and later descent calculations, but those contextual links do not resolve which punctures and which covering category the source intends.

relation: Restates the diagram; earlier and later context add related constructions; the unpunctured local model exposes an unresolved interpretation.

title: Distinguish the line-bundle root gerbe from the divisor root stack
place: Kummer algebra and Chern target; normal-bundle class
source_words: de type Kummérien; la classe de Chern; fibré normal
body: The source's local Kummer equations and Chern-class target suggest separating two objects that Hua's later root-stack interpretation puts close together: the gerbe of roots of a line bundle and the root stack of its defining section. For X=Spec k[x], D=(x), and n>1 invertible in k, the divisor root stack [Spec k[z]/μₙ], x=zⁿ, has trivial stabilizer off D and μₙ at D, whereas the root gerbe of the trivial line bundle O_X(D) is Bμₙ everywhere. This explicit distinction refines the modern comparison and suggests tracking the section as well as the line bundle; it does not establish an equivalence with the archival covering category or a novelty claim.

title: The general Kummer programme needs a topology convention
place: allowed tame roots of unity; arbitrary n_i and degree-two class
source_words: n_i entiers ≥1; H²(X,μ_n); On veut prouver
body: Scan101 allows arbitrary positive exponents before asking for the Kummer–Chern equality, whereas the tame examples restrict the permitted residue characteristics. The Kummer sequence is exact on the fppf site for every positive n, and its usual étale surjectivity requires n invertible; the finite free root algebra and the derivative criterion verify that distinction. Hua's earlier Kummer data and later ‘Le boitement, avoué’ add the same branchwise characteristic issue, so any proof of the proposed variants should name its topology and coefficient hypotheses explicitly.

title: Pro-representing finite cohomology coefficients is a different finite-model problem
body: A useful comparison with RESULTS_STATE is to keep the test categories explicit: scan105 proposes a pro-group representing H² on finite abelian coefficient groups, whereas FINMON C2-CP2 asks about finite categories realizing a homotopy type and S2COUNT concerns maps from finite tests to spheres. Hua's ‘π₂’ and later ‘Quand un foncteur est pro-représentable’ supply a methodological link through functors and pro-objects, but they do not identify these different representability demands. No conclusion about either registered finite-model problem follows from the source's one-line pro-representability claim.

title: The field-group and variable-base-group categories must remain separate
place: exact functor setup and subsequent admissible-group fibre product
source_words: exactitude de F; S-groupes admissibles; le produit fibré
body: The contrast between the letter's exact-functor setting and arbitrary admissible S-group morphisms is also the right point for a literature comparison. Antei's ‘On the bumpy fundamental group scheme’, §2.2 and §3, distinguishes finite k-group torsors from a relative base and expressly identifies nonflat group fibre products as an obstruction in the latter setting. That warning agrees with the independently checked cusp obstruction here, but it neither proves the archival restart nor resolves LM1 E.11, and no assertion about the current status of every relative fundamental-group problem is inferred from this 2015 paper.

External comparison: [Antei, arXiv:1511.07331v1, §2.2–3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1511.07331).
relation: Context adds the restricted categorical restart; the primary literature supplies a matching warning rather than a proof of this manuscript statement.

title: Reducedness remains essential for the stated pointed rigidity
place: provisional condition (vi); Proposition3 and pointed automorphisms
source_words: essentiellement provisoires; S réduit connexe; Aut(P,ξ)
body: The kernel-uniqueness check should not be used to remove reducedness from the separate rigidity claim on scans126 and138. Over S=Spec k[ε]/(ε²) in characteristic p>0, the trivial α_p-torsor has distinct sections0 and ε with the same value at its geometric point, and translation by ε is a nonidentity equivariant automorphism fixing that marking. This refutes the version with reducedness omitted and sharpens the distinction in Hua's ‘Le dispositif’ and ‘Les groupes admissibles’, while leaving the source's qualified assertion intact.

relation: Adds a counterexample to dropping reducedness; complements rather than contradicts the qualified source statement.
reason: The two sections and pointed translation are checked directly in k[ε]/(ε²), with ε^p=0 and ε nonzero.
